selftext:
Halcyon FX week 5 live: 5 trades, +$14.80, and both losses came from exits rather than entries

>Disclosure: I built this EA and sell it.  
>  
>Weekly update on my MT5 supply/demand EA, live on a small account since mid-September. I post every week, losing weeks included. It's been about a year in development with many iterations, but these numbers are only from the current live run.  
>  
>**Setup:** about a $1,079 LIVE account, 0.01–0.08 lots. It trades H1 supply/demand zones with M15 confirmation and needs H4 to agree. A local AI check (Claude) can veto entries but never opens trades.

>**Changes:** none during the week. Going into this week, I'm loading a fix that stops rollover spread spikes from triggering stops, plus a fix for a bug where editing a trade by hand broke the risk calculation. Two ideas I tested and rejected: moving the stop to +0.25R at +1R (cut tester results from +17.25R to +10.46R over 74 trades), and loosening the entry filters (it lost money).

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: How will the rollover-spike fix protect the position without turning the broker-side stop into a wider or virtual stop? The GBPCAD quote jumping about 30 pips is a useful test case: replay the actual bid/ask around rollover and show whether the revised logic would still exit during a genuine gap, terminal disconnect, or EA restart. I’d add the hand-edited NZDUSD stop and the risk-calculation bug to the same regression suite, verifying that every manual modification immediately recomputes worst-case account exposure. Claude’s entry veto cannot mitigate either failure mode, so execution safeguards deserve separate reporting.

replies.author: Teh_Eno
replies.body:
Fair challenge, and agreed: the AI veto does nothing for execution risk, so I'll report execution safeguards separately.

How the rollover fix works (live since 19 Oct): the broker-side SL is never removed. During the short rollover window it's widened by a capped buffer, while the EA holds the real stop internally and closes at market if price actually hits it. The widened broker SL also follows the internal stop and only ever tightens, then goes back to normal after the window.

What it doesn't cover:

* If the terminal is offline or restarting during the window, only the broker SL protects the trade, so the worst case is the stop plus the buffer, capped around 0.75R.
* A real price gap fills wherever the broker fills it, like any stop.
* If price is already too close to the stop at rollover, the broker won't allow the widen, so a spread spike can still hit it. That happened on AUDUSD this week and it's under review.

I haven't done a tick-level bid/ask replay of the GBPCAD spike yet. It was checked with tester replays, and your suggestion is a better test, so I'll add it.

On the NZDUSD hand edit: R is now measured against each trade's original 1R risk. Recomputing account-wide worst-case exposure after a manual edit isn't covered by this fix, and it's a good one for the regression list.
